To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a U-shape relationship was seen between the sleep duration and mortality, with the lowest mortality at a sleep duration of 6.5-9 hours.

a U-shaped association between sleep duration and all-cause mortality was found, with a lower risk at sleep duration of approximately 7 hours, and that the risk of death was increased among persons with short and long sleep durations.
a U-shaped relationship between sleep duration with all-cause and disease-specific mortality was observed in a large prospective Korean cohort study.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the relationship between sleep duration, mortality and disease-specific mortality.
the relationship of sleep durations with all-cause and disease-specific mortality.
the effects of sleep duration on all-cause and disease-specific mortality, and it is the first study to examine the relationship of sleep durations with mortality in Korea.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the optimal sleep duration is 7 to 9 hours, and that sleep duration outside this range may be associated with a higher risk of mortality.
sleep duration of 5 to 10 hours may be recommended for a general healthy population.
sleep durations of 7 hours may be recommended for a healthy lifestyle in Korea.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a healthy sleep duration is associated inversely with all-cause mortality in a large cohort study.
a short sleep duration of ≤ 5 hours is related to a higher risk of mortality in Korea.
a sleep duration of 6 hours is associated with an increased risk of all-cause and disease-specific mortality.
The main takeaway from our work is that
sleep duration should be considered as an important parameter in the management of patients.
sleep duration of 6 to 8 hours is associated with a lower risk of mortality in the general population.
sleep duration of 6 to 8 hours is associated with the lowest risk of all-cause mortality in the general population.
